title: Bias-Aware Adversarial Toxicity Classifier
summary: Text is normalized by replacing URLs, emails and mentions with markers, then tokenized and truncated. Standardized length, character, punctuation and style features are computed. Hash-based splitting keeps duplicate raw comments in one partition. A partially frozen pretrained DistilRoBERTa encoder provides a first-token representation; a gated numeric-feature MLP is fused with it before a shared MLP and toxicity, auxiliary-toxicity and identity heads. Identity prediction uses toxicity-conditioned features through gradient reversal. The model also accepts the training toxicity target as conditioning input. Weighted BCE emphasizes subgroup, non-toxic subgroup and toxic non-subgroup examples; auxiliary and identity BCE are applied where labels exist. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine decay. Length-bucketed padded batches reduce padding. Validation uses sigmoid logits and a bias-aware AUC aggregate for checkpointing and early stopping; the selected model writes clipped test probabilities.

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized by replacing URLs, emails and mentions, removing HTML, and computing numeric text features. An exact-comment hash split keeps duplicates together. Tokenized text (maximum 256 tokens) is dynamically padded and length-bucketed. A DeBERTa-v3-large first-token representation is gated with an MLP encoding numeric features; a shared MLP produces toxicity, six auxiliary toxicity, and identity-adversary logits. Gradient reversal sends shared features and a toxicity condition to the identity adversary. Training minimizes weighted binary cross-entropy for continuous toxicity, emphasizing non-toxic identity and toxic non-identity examples, plus weighted auxiliary and identity losses. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. Checkpoints and early stopping use a bias-aware AUC score combining overall and subgroup-related power means. The best checkpoint produces clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities for CSV output.

title: Bias-aware dual-view ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML-normalized; URLs, emails and IPs are replaced with tokens. Regex identity detection creates identity-tagged and identity-masked views, while 12 standardized style features are computed. Toxicity is binarized at 0.5. Grouped stratified 10-fold splitting uses raw-comment hashes to keep duplicates within one partition; strata combine toxicity and rare identity labels. A frozen pretrained ModernBERT encodes original text and, for identity-containing comments, masked text with 128-token truncation. First-token embeddings are concatenated with a trainable style projection and passed to a dropout MLP producing toxicity and six auxiliary logits. Identity-row logits mix original and masked predictions with masked weight 0.60. Loss combines weighted toxicity BCE, auxiliary BCE, identity-specific weighting, and a clean-identity squared counterfactual consistency penalty. AdamW uses encoder/head parameter groups, cosine warmup, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping and early stopping. Checkpoints use overall and subgroup ROC-AUC; inference sigmoids and clips toxicity probabilities.

title: Dual-view bias-aware ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The system predicts toxicity from normalized comments using a pretrained ModernBERT encoder and standardized 12-dimensional style features. It forms original, identity-tagged, and identity-masked text views through Unicode/HTML normalization, marker replacement for URLs, emails and IPs, lexical identity regexes, and whitespace cleanup. Original and masked views are tokenized to 256 tokens; the model combines each CLS embedding with projected style features and outputs a toxicity logit plus six auxiliary logits. For lexically identity-related comments, inference interpolates original- and masked-view toxicity logits; otherwise it uses the original view. Training uses grouped 10-fold splits based on comment hashes, stratified by toxicity and rare identity membership. The loss combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, identity-related weighting, and raw/masked prediction consistency for clean identity comments. AdamW uses separate encoder and head learning rates, cosine warmup, mixed precision where available, gradient accumulation, and clipping. Checkpoints are selected using a fairness-aware ROC-AUC; clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities are written in test ID order.

title: Bias-aware ModernBERT toxicity classification
summary: A ModernBERT-large classifier predicts a primary toxicity logit and six subtype logits. Text is HTML/Unicode-normalized, stripped of zero-width characters, URLs and emails replaced, whitespace cleaned and truncated; an alternative robust view lowercases, deobfuscates spaced letters and selected leetspeak, and compresses repeated characters. Inputs retain head and tail content before 512-token tokenization. Group-aware article-level validation splitting targets toxicity and identity prevalence. Training combines weighted BCE for fractional toxicity labels and subtype BCE with identity-aware pairwise softplus ranking losses; identity-group losses are softmax-weighted toward difficult groups. Identity-associated non-toxic samples receive higher weights, with modest toxic-sample upweighting. Batches are shuffled, use mixed precision, gradient accumulation and norm clipping. AdamW uses layer-wise learning-rate decay, a higher classifier-head rate, selected no-decay parameters, and cosine warmup/decay scheduling. Checkpoints and early stopping use validation bias score. Best-checkpoint inference applies sigmoid to the primary logit, sanitizes and clips probabilities, and writes ID-prediction output.

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized with URL, email and mention markers, then paired with standardized text statistics. Exact-comment hashes form an approximately 80/20 duplicate-group train/validation split. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes up to 256 tokens. Its first-token embedding is fused through gating with an MLP over numeric text features, then a shared MLP produces a primary toxicity logit, six auxiliary toxicity logits, and an identity adversary conditioned on toxicity probability via gradient reversal. Loss combines weighted BCE for continuous primary toxicity labels, auxiliary BCE, and identity BCE where labels are available; weights emphasize identity non-toxic and non-identity toxic samples. Length-bucketed batches use dynamic padding. AdamW applies separate backbone and head learning rates, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine decay. Checkpoints are selected by a bias-aware ROC-AUC aggregate over overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP metrics. Inference sigmoid-transforms, clips, and writes row-aligned predictions with test IDs.

title: Identity-masked bias-aware ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML-normalized; URLs, emails and IPs are replaced with markers. Regex identity flags create an identity-masked text view, and 12 standardized style features are derived. A ModernBERT-base model encodes original text and masked text for lexical-identity examples; CLS embeddings are combined with projected style features to predict toxicity and six auxiliary labels. Identity examples blend original and masked logits with masked weight 0.60. Training uses weighted toxicity BCE, upweighting clean and toxic identity examples, masked auxiliary BCE for finite labels, and a counterfactual squared probability-difference penalty for clean identity comments. Dynamic tokenization truncates views to 256 tokens. The first fold of stratified group cross-validation is used, with duplicate-comment hashes held within partitions and scaling fit on training data. AdamW uses separate encoder/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, checkpointing and early stopping. Inference reloads the selected checkpoint, sigmoid-transforms and clips toxicity logits, then writes ordered predictions.

title: Bias-aware ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are normalized with URL/email markers and engineered text statistics. Duplicate texts are group-split into stratified train/validation partitions. Training includes identity-word-swapped augmentations whose identity labels are masked. A pretrained ModernBERT-large classifier, with dropout and an eight-logit output head, tokenizes padded/truncated text and predicts toxicity plus auxiliary labels. The objective combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, identity-specific pairwise softplus ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN and BNSP comparisons, and Smooth L1 alignment of subgroup/background non-toxic mean logits. Group losses use temperature-controlled log-sum-exp; ranking pairs may be subsampled. Batches cover identity/background and toxic/non-toxic strata before global shuffled examples. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, excludes bias and normalization parameters from weight decay, and is paired with mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, cosine warmup, and optional checkpointing. Checkpoints use a bias-aware AUC; inference sigmoids toxicity logits and writes test predictions.

title: ModernBERT Weighted Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes ModernBERT-large for binary toxicity prediction with one logit per comment. Text is Unicode-normalized, HTML-unescaped, stripped of controls and excess whitespace, and has URLs, emails and mentions replaced by markers. Ten standardized count/ratio features are computed, but their connection to model inputs is not shown. Grouped stratified 10-fold splitting keeps identical raw comments within one fold using toxicity-by-identity strata. Soft fractional toxicity labels are optimized with weighted binary cross-entropy; weights combine natural sampling and uniform stratum balancing. Batches use dynamic padding and truncation to 192 tokens. AdamW assigns separate backbone and classifier learning rates, with mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, activation checkpointing, and linear warmup/decay. Validation selects checkpoints using an equally weighted bias-aware AUC metric. The best checkpoint is reloaded, sigmoid converts logits to probabilities, and test ID/probability pairs are saved.

title: ModernBERT Weighted Toxicity Classifier
summary: A ModernBERT-large sequence classifier is fine-tuned to predict scalar comment toxicity. Raw comments are grouped to prevent duplicate leakage in a grouped 10-fold split; fold 0 is validation, with strata defined from toxicity and identity information. Text is Unicode-normalized and HTML-unescaped, while URLs, emails and mentions are replaced with markers and empty inputs are explicitly marked. Comments are tokenized and truncated to 256 tokens. Soft toxicity labels are trained using weighted binary cross-entropy on logits. Training allocation mixes uniform row probability with equal probability across four strata, using a sampler that visits each row once per epoch. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, linear warmup/decay, gradient accumulation, optional float16 AMP, gradient clipping, and scheduler updates after optimizer steps. Validation uses overall and identity-related generalized AUC components; the best checkpoint is saved, reloaded, and used for final validation and sigmoid-based test prediction. Test IDs and probabilities are written to a submission file.

title: ModernBERT weighted toxicity classifier
summary: A ModernBERT-base sequence classifier is fine-tuned to predict continuous toxicity probabilities. Comments are Unicode-normalized and HTML-decoded; URLs, emails, and mentions are replaced with markers, while control characters and excess whitespace are removed. Duplicate-grouped stratified 10-fold splitting uses toxicity-by-identity strata. Fractional targets are optimized with sample-weighted binary cross-entropy on logits. Training sampling mixes natural sampling (70%) and equal-stratum sampling (30%), with non-repeating stratum-prioritized ordering. Inputs are truncated to 192 tokens and dynamically padded. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, weight decay, linear warmup/decay, accumulation, gradient clipping, mixed precision, and activation checkpointing. Validation combines overall AUC with power-mean subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP AUCs; the best checkpoint is retained and reloaded. Sigmoid probabilities are generated for test inputs and saved with input IDs.

title: Identity-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized and cleaned, with URLs/emails replaced, and text-derived features computed. A grouped, stratified validation split uses toxicity and identity presence. Training adds lexical identity-swap counterfactuals while retaining toxicity and auxiliary labels but removing identity labels. A pretrained ModernBERT classifier produces toxicity plus six auxiliary logits; the encoder is frozen and the classifier head uses dropout when available. The objective combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, identity-specific subgroup/BPSN/BNSP pairwise ranking losses, temperature log-sum-exp aggregation across identities, and Smooth-L1 alignment of non-toxic subgroup and background logits. Tokenization uses truncation and dynamic padding. Identity/toxicity-stratified batches are used with AdamW parameter groups, cosine warmup scheduling, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and clipping. Checkpoints are selected from overall and identity AUC power means. Test toxicity probabilities are sigmoid-transformed, clipped, and exported to CSV.

title: Bias-resistant DeBERTa toxicity classification
summary: Comments are normalized by masking URLs, emails and mentions and limiting character elongation. Gender, race, religion and sexuality word swaps create counterfactual texts. Standardized style features cover length, capitalization, punctuation, digits and elongation. Duplicate-normalized texts are kept together in a forward temporal split. DeBERTa-v3-large encodes tokenized text; its first-token representation is layer-normalized and fused with a learned style embedding. Toxicity, auxiliary attribute and adversarial identity heads are trained with weighted masked BCE, including increased weights for identity-related examples; gradient reversal suppresses identity information. Scheduled counterfactual batches add Smooth-L1 consistency between original and swapped toxicity probabilities. Training uses shuffled data, dynamic padding, AdamW with separate backbone/head rates, AMP, accumulation, finite-loss checks, clipping, warmup/linear decay, and early stopping on bias-aware AUC combining overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP AUCs. Selected checkpoints output clipped test probabilities.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized, cleaned of HTML, URLs and emails, and accompanied by engineered text statistics. A group-held-out validation split is stratified by toxicity and identity evaluation. Training combines original rows with identity-term counterfactual swaps; swapped rows retain toxicity and auxiliary targets while identity labels are cleared. ModernBERT produces seven logits for toxicity and six auxiliary attributes, with a replaced classifier head, 0.15 dropout, and a frozen encoder. The objective combines identity-weighted primary toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, identity-aware pairwise ranking over subgroup/background positive and negative strata, and non-toxic subgroup calibration; ranking terms use temperature-controlled log-sum-exp. Batches preferentially include unused examples from each identity/background-by-label stratum before shuffled filling. AdamW, cosine warmup scheduling, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and clipping are used. Checkpoints are selected by a combined overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP validation AUC. Sigmoid toxicity probabilities are clipped and exported after submission-ID validation.

title: DistilBERT Toxicity Prediction Pipeline
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, unescapes HTML, replaces URLs, emails and mentions with tokens, removes tags and normalizes whitespace. It creates toxicity and identity indicators by thresholding labels at 0.5, and uses a grouped stratified split so exact duplicate raw comments do not cross folds. A pretrained DistilBERT classifier with one output is fine-tuned on continuous toxicity targets using per-example binary cross-entropy with logits. Training samples are drawn with replacement using clipped inverse-frequency weights across target and identity-presence cells. Text is dynamically padded and truncated to 96 tokens. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, excludes bias and normalization parameters from weight decay, and uses mixed precision, gradient accumulation, gradient clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Validation computes overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP AUC metrics. The best checkpoint is reloaded for validation and test sigmoid probabilities, which are checked and written with IDs to CSV.

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The pipeline normalizes comment text, replaces URLs, emails and long numbers with markers, and derives ten standardized style/count features. It uses an article-disjoint validation split balanced for toxicity and identity prevalence. Dynamically tokenized text is encoded by DeBERTa-v3-large; CLS and masked-mean embeddings are fused with projected numeric features. The model predicts toxicity, six auxiliary labels, and nine identities through a gradient-reversal adversarial head. Its criterion combines subgroup-upweighted toxicity BCE, auxiliary and masked identity BCE, and subgroup/BPSN/BNSP pairwise ranking losses. Training uses shuffled seeded batches, optional gradient checkpointing, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, AdamW with layer-wise encoder learning-rate decay and higher head rate, plus cosine scheduling with 6% warmup. The adversarial coefficient follows a logistic ramp to 0.20 and is zero at inference. Early stopping and checkpointing use a generalized-mean ROC-AUC metric across overall and bias subsets; the best checkpoint outputs sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classification
summary: The solution normalizes comment text with Unicode normalization, HTML unescaping, placeholder replacement for URLs, emails and mentions, tag removal, and whitespace cleanup. It derives identity-related features and splits data with StratifiedGroupKFold, stratifying toxicity and identity-label state while grouping duplicate raw comments. Training samples are reweighted with replacement to balance toxicity-by-identity-presence cells. A ModernBERT-base sequence classifier produces one logit and is fine-tuned on continuous toxicity targets using unreduced binary cross-entropy with logits. Inputs are truncated to 128 tokens and dynamically padded. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, excluding biases and normalization parameters from weight decay. Training uses checkpointing, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Validation computes overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP AUCs using a negative-power mean. The best checkpoint is reloaded for validation and test inference; sigmoid probabilities are checked and written as id/prediction CSV output.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Regression Training
summary: Text comments are Unicode-normalized, HTML-unescaped, stripped of tags, replaced with URL, email and mention placeholders, and whitespace-normalized. Text statistics and thresholded toxicity/identity indicators are derived. A duplicate-grouped, toxicity-by-identity stratified split is used. Training examples are sampled with replacement using weights that balance toxicity and identity-presence cells. ModernBERT-large produces one logit per 192-token input; BCE-with-logits is applied per example to continuous toxicity targets. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, with bias and normalization parameters exempted from weight decay. Training uses mixed precision, gradient scaling, accumulation, unscaling, global norm clipping, optimizer steps, linear warmup and cosine decay. Validation computes overall, subgroup, BPSN and BNSP AUC components with a negative-power mean metric. The best checkpoint is restored for validation and test sigmoid probabilities; submissions are checked for row count, required columns, and finite nonmissing predictions before CSV export.

title: Hierarchical ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized, HTML-decoded, anonymized for URLs, emails and users, and whitespace-cleaned. Count, ratio, and short/empty-text numeric features are derived. A forward time-based validation split, with ID fallback, keeps duplicate normalized texts in validation. ModernBERT tokenizes each comment into up to two overlapping 256-token windows with stride 64. Masked mean-pooled window embeddings are attention-aggregated and concatenated with an MLP encoding numeric features to produce a toxicity logit. Training uses soft-label BCE combined with GroupDRO over the overall population and available identity subgroup positive/negative partitions, with adaptive softmax group weights. Batches pad selected windows and include identity annotations. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates, weight decay, AMP, accumulation, clipping, warmup-cosine scheduling, and optional checkpointing. Checkpoints use an identity-aware AUC metric; inference reloads the best model, applies sigmoid, and writes ID-indexed predictions.

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comments by replacing URLs, emails and long numbers, and derives ten standardized style and length features. Missing text and labels are zero-filled. An article-disjoint validation split is balanced for toxicity and identity prevalence. Dynamically padded, truncated token sequences and numeric features enter a DeBERTa-v3-large encoder; CLS and masked-mean embeddings are fused with a projected numeric embedding. The shared representation produces a toxicity logit, six auxiliary-label outputs, and identity predictions through a gradient-reversal adversary for nine identities. Training combines subgroup-upweighted BCE for continuous toxicity, auxiliary and observed-identity BCE, and softplus pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN and BNSP cases. AdamW uses layer-wise encoder learning-rate decay, higher head rates, selective weight decay, AMP, checkpointing, gradient accumulation and norm clipping, with cosine decay and 6% warmup. The adversarial coefficient follows a capped logistic ramp and is disabled at inference. The selected checkpoint maximizes an AUC-based validation metric; sigmoid toxicity probabilities are clipped and written by test ID.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comments, computes 14 standardized lexical features, and splits data by normalized-text hash with toxicity and identity stratification. A ModernBERT-large encoder mean-pools masked token embeddings. A numeric-feature MLP is sigmoid-gated and residually fused with the text representation, then feeds toxicity, auxiliary-toxicity, and identity heads. Inputs are tokenized with fixed-length truncation, padding, attention masks, and float numeric features. Training uses weighted BCE for continuous toxicity targets, masked BCE for auxiliary and identity labels, and pairwise softplus ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP fairness pairs. Identity-annotated, especially non-toxic subgroup, samples receive higher toxicity-loss weights. AdamW uses lower encoder learning rates, decay exemptions for biases and normalization, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and cosine warmup scheduling. Checkpoints are selected by a bias-aware AUC combining overall and power-mean subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP AUCs; best-model test probabilities are clipped and saved with submission IDs.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Ranker with Feature Fusion
summary: The solution normalizes comment text and derives 13 standardized text-statistic features. Exact duplicate raw comments are kept within train or validation groups, and splits are stratified by binary toxicity and a primary official identity group. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes dynamically padded, truncated tokens. CLS and masked-mean embeddings are concatenated and projected; projected numeric features are added through a sigmoid gate. The fused representation produces toxicity and six subtype logits. Training uses annotator-count-weighted BCE on continuous toxicity, masked subtype BCE, and pairwise subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP ranking losses across official identities, with hard-group aggregation. AdamW uses separate backbone and head rates and excludes bias and normalization parameters from decay. It uses shuffled batches, mixed precision, accumulation, gradient clipping, and warmup followed by cosine decay. Checkpoints are selected by combined overall and identity AUC metrics; early stopping is used. Best-model test probabilities are clipped and written by submission ID.

title: Fairness-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text through Unicode and HTML processing, control-character removal, URL/email replacement and whitespace cleanup, then computes 12 surface features. Duplicate-text groups and toxicity/identity strata define grouped five-fold splits. Training adds identity-term counterfactual swaps with retained toxicity/subtype labels but disabled identity supervision. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder supplies masked-mean embeddings, fused with an MLP representation of surface features. Heads predict toxicity, six toxicity subtypes and nine identities; the identity head uses gradient-reversed semantic features. Weighted binary cross-entropy combines main, auxiliary and masked identity-adversarial losses, with fairness weights emphasizing identity-related cases. Tokenization uses truncation, dynamic padding and length-bucketed batches. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates, selective weight decay, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation and gradient clipping. Checkpoints use validation bias-aware AUC. Inference disables gradient reversal, applies sigmoid to toxicity logits, restores row order and writes clipped probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are cleaned by replacing URLs and emails and converted into surface features covering length, capitalization, punctuation, digits, profanity cues and identity-term counts. A group-stratified validation split keeps duplicate cleaned texts together while stratifying by toxicity and nine identity labels. Lower-weight counterfactual examples are generated by swapping annotated identity terms while preserving toxicity and auxiliary targets. A DeBERTa-v3-small encoder mean-pools token embeddings; an MLP encodes surface features, and concatenated representations feed toxicity and six auxiliary heads. A gradient-reversal adversary predicts nine identities from semantic features. Training combines weighted toxicity BCE-with-logits, averaged auxiliary BCE, and masked identity adversarial BCE; identity-related samples receive increased fairness weights, while counterfactuals disable identity supervision. Dynamic truncated tokenization and length-bucketed shuffled batches are used. AdamW, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine decay optimize the model. Reloaded selected checkpoints produce clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized through Unicode and HTML processing, control-character removal, URL/email replacement, and whitespace cleanup. Text-derived numeric features cover length, casing, punctuation, digits, profanity cues, and identity-term counts. Grouped stratified folds use normalized duplicate texts and toxicity/identity strata. Identity-term counterfactual swaps can augment training while preserving toxicity and subtype labels; identity supervision is masked for these rows. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder is masked-mean pooled and fused with an MLP over surface features to predict toxicity and six auxiliary subtypes. A gradient-reversal identity head predicts nine identity attributes from semantic features. Weighted binary cross-entropy combines main, auxiliary, and masked adversarial losses, with fairness-oriented example weighting. Dynamic truncated tokenization, length-bucketed batching, AdamW with separate encoder/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, and optional checkpointing are used. Checkpoints use a bias-aware AUC aggregate; inference sigmoids toxicity logits and clips written predictions.

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Ranker
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized, cleaned of zero-width characters, URLs, emails and HTML, with repeated punctuation limited; 13 standardized text-statistic features are created. Duplicate raw comments are grouped during stratified splitting by toxicity and primary identity where possible. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder yields CLS and masked mean embeddings, which are concatenated, projected, and sigmoid-gated with projected numeric features. The fused representation predicts toxicity and six subtype logits. Training combines annotator-confidence-weighted BCE for continuous toxicity, masked subtype BCE, and differentiable pairwise ranking losses for identity subgroup, BPSN and BNSP sets, aggregated with a power mean. AdamW uses lower encoder learning rates, excluded decay for bias/normalization parameters, AMP, checkpointing, accumulation, clipping, warmup and cosine scheduling. Checkpoints are selected by a bias-aware AUC score; test toxicity sigmoid outputs are clipped and saved with IDs.

title: Bias-aware DeBERTa toxicity ranker
summary: Comments are canonicalized with Unicode normalization, URL/email masking, HTML and zero-width-character removal, repeated-punctuation limiting, and 13 standardized style features. Duplicate-grouped validation splitting is stratified by binary toxicity and primary identity. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3 encoder combines projected CLS and masked-mean embeddings with sigmoid-gated numeric features, then predicts toxicity and six subtype logits. Training uses annotator-count-weighted toxicity BCE, masked subtype BCE, and differentiable pairwise ranking losses for identity subgroups and BPSN/BNSP pair types, with a power mean over group losses. AdamW applies lower backbone than head learning rates and excludes bias/normalization parameters from weight decay. Mini-batch training supports mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping, 3% warmup plus cosine decay, and early stopping using bias-aware validation AUC. The selected checkpoint outputs sigmoid toxicity probabilities, clipped and aligned to submission IDs.

title: Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML-normalized, with URLs and users replaced, control characters removed, and whitespace compressed. Twelve robust-scaled text-shape features capture length, casing, punctuation, and identity-term counts. A DeBERTa-v3-large first-token representation is projected and concatenated with a numeric-feature adapter for binary toxicity prediction. A gradient-reversal identity multilabel adversary promotes identity-invariant representations. Training uses positive-weighted toxicity BCE plus 0.08 masked identity BCE, excluding missing identity labels. Rows are sampled with replacement from four toxicity/identity buckets using allocated mass; selected benign identity texts receive identity-word-swap counterfactuals. A Smooth L1 term aligns factual and counterfactual toxicity probabilities. The adversarial scale ramps during training. AdamW uses lower encoder learning rates, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, and scaler updates. Inference returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities; validation computes subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP ROC-AUC diagnostics.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Identity-Cell DRO
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, tokenizes it to 256 tokens, and computes ten standardized structural text features. A two-class DeBERTa-v3-large classifier combines text logits with a LayerNorm-MLP structural-feature adapter through a learned bounded scale. Continuous toxicity labels are thresholded at 0.5. Sample weights balance classes and emphasize identity-related and non-toxic identity examples. Training minimizes weighted global binary cross-entropy plus Group-DRO across four toxicity/identity cells for each selected identity; exponential-moving-average cell losses define softmax group weights. Shuffled, seeded batches use custom collation and drop incomplete batches. AdamW uses separate learning rates for encoder and other parameters, decoupled weight decay, AMP, gradient checkpointing, gradient accumulation, and gradient clipping at norm 1.0. Learning rate follows linear warmup then cosine decay with a 0.25 minimum multiplier. Checkpoints restore model and criterion states. Inference returns the class-1 softmax probability using saved feature-normalization state.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Structural Features
summary: The solution normalizes comments using HTML unescaping, NFKC normalization, tag removal, URL replacement, repeated-punctuation limiting, and whitespace collapsing. It computes and standardizes ten structural features, then combines tokenized text (maximum 256 tokens) with these features in a pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large two-class classifier. Structural features pass through layer normalization and an MLP; their logits are added to encoder logits through a learned bounded scale. Binary cross-entropy is applied to the positive-minus-negative logit difference for continuous toxicity targets. Sample weights balance classes and emphasize identity-related and non-toxic identity examples. The objective combines weighted global loss with Group-DRO over toxicity/identity cells, using EMA cell losses and temperature-softmax group weights. AdamW uses a lower encoder learning rate, linear warm-up then cosine decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and norm-1 clipping. Inference returns softmax probability for class 1; checkpoints retain model, criterion, tokenizer, and feature-normalization state.

title: Adversarial Counterfactual DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments undergo Unicode/HTML normalization, URL and user replacement, and whitespace cleanup. Twelve robustly scaled text-shape features are combined with text tokenized to 256 tokens. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder’s first-token representation is projected and fused with a 96-dimensional numeric-feature adapter to produce a toxicity logit. A gradient-reversed head predicts 24 identity attributes, with its adversarial scale ramped from 0.05 toward 1 across optimizer steps. Training uses continuous toxicity labels and masked missing identity labels; benign identity comments can receive swapped-identity counterfactual text. The loss combines positive-weighted toxicity binary cross-entropy, weighted masked multilabel identity BCE, and, when pairs exist, a weighted Smooth L1 consistency penalty between factual and counterfactual toxicity probabilities. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates with no decay for bias/normalization parameters. AMP, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, and scaler-managed updates are used. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text by HTML unescaping, NFKC conversion, zero-width-character removal, URL/user replacement, and whitespace collapsing. It combines a ModernBERT first-token embedding with a gated two-layer 128-dimensional encoder for scaled numeric style and lexical features, then predicts toxicity and auxiliary labels. Toxicity targets are binarized at 0.5. Training uses normalized bias-aware example weights and combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, and subgroup BPSN ranking loss aggregated by a negative-power generalized mean. Batches cycle through identity groups, pairing non-toxic subgroup examples with toxic non-subgroup comparators before weighted random filling. Text is truncated to 256 tokens and dynamically padded. AdamW applies lower encoder learning rates and omits bias/normalization parameters from weight decay. AMP training accumulates gradients over two batches and clips norms to 1.0. Inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits; validation reports overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP AUC diagnostics.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classification Pipeline
summary: The solution normalizes comment text through HTML unescaping, NFKC normalization, zero-width-character removal, and URL/user placeholders. It derives style, lexical-toxicity, and identity features, log-transforms count features, and robust-scales numeric inputs from training data. A ModernBERT-large encoder’s first-token representation is fused with a gated MLP encoding numeric features, then feeds primary toxicity and auxiliary multi-label heads. Primary labels are thresholded at 0.5. Training uses example-weighted binary cross-entropy, masked auxiliary BCE, and sampled pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP slices, combined by temperature-controlled log-sum-exp. title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Group-DRO

A two-class DeBERTa-v3-large model tokenizes comments dynamically to 256 tokens and predicts toxicity. Labels threshold toxicity at 0.5; identity annotations define subgroup and background slices. The objective combines binary cross-entropy on the toxic/non-toxic logit margin (weight 0.60) with a hard-weighted pairwise ranking loss (0.40) over subgroup, background-positive/subgroup-negative, and subgroup-positive/background-negative slices, sampling up to 96 positive-negative pairs per slice deterministically. Only the classifier/pooler and encoder layers 18–23 are trainable. AdamW uses 1.5e-5 for encoder parameters and 5e-5 for head parameters. Training uses shuffled batches, mixed precision, gradient scaling, unscaling, global gradient clipping at norm 1.0, and scaler-mediated updates. Inference returns class-1 softmax probability.

title: Conditional MMD DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution predicts continuous toxicity probabilities from comment text with a DeBERTa-based model. It splits data before preprocessing, normalizes text, replaces URLs, derives count, ratio, punctuation and identity-lexicon features, and creates identity-masked text; the shown neural input uses tokenized model text truncated to 256 tokens. The encoder’s first-token representation is layer-normalized, dropped out, and passed through a GELU MLP to produce one logit. Training batches contain toxicity and nine identity targets. The loss combines binary cross-entropy with 0.03-weighted conditional MMD, aligning random-Fourier-feature logit distributions between identity-present and identity-absent samples separately within benign and toxic strata. AdamW uses distinct encoder and head learning rates. Training supports mixed precision, gradient accumulation, unscaling, norm clipping at 1.0, and GradScaler updates. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities. Checkpoints preserve model, optimizer, tokenizer, configuration, metadata, and optional feature manifests.

title: Fairness-Weighted ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a ModernBERT-large sequence classifier with one logit for continuous toxicity targets. It splits data before preprocessing, normalizes comment text with HTML decoding, NFKC normalization, URL/email placeholders, and whitespace/control-character cleanup. It computes and standardizes auxiliary text statistics, but the saved inference state specifies that these numeric features are not used by the model. Targets and nine identity indicators are clipped to [0,1] and binarized at 0.5. Training examples in identity-by-toxicity strata receive train-only inverse-prevalence weights, clipped to 1–6 and combined by maximum. Tokenized text is truncated to 256 tokens. The objective is weighted binary cross-entropy with logits against soft targets. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates and decay groups. Training runs up to two shuffled epochs with mixed precision, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, and runtime-controlled stopping. Inference applies sigmoid probabilities to batched tokenized text.

title: Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized with NFKC, HTML decoding/removal, URL and email replacement, control-character removal, and whitespace collapsing, then tokenized to 256 tokens. The dataset also derives identity-masked text and standardized style features, but the described model input uses normalized text. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large encoder is mean-pooled over non-padding tokens and passed through linear, LayerNorm, GELU, and dropout layers to toxicity, subtype, and identity heads. Training minimizes identity-upweighted binary toxicity loss, masked subtype BCE, and benign-example identity BCE through gradient reversal; unavailable subtype or identity labels are masked. Shuffled batches use custom collation. AdamW applies separate backbone and head learning rates with decay exclusions. CUDA AMP, gradient scaling, accumulation, and gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 are used before updates. Checkpoints store model, tokenizer, and style scaler. Inference batches normalized text, sigmoid-transforms toxicity logits, and clips outputs to [0,1].

title: Dual-window ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are normalized with Unicode NFKC, HTML decoding/removal, control-character cleanup, URL/user placeholders, lowercasing, and style-prefix tokens. Nine standardized surface features are derived. A pretrained ModernBERT encodes separate first and last 190-token windows; normalized CLS vectors are attention-gated and pooled, concatenated with numeric features, and passed through a fusion MLP with heads for toxicity and six subtype targets. Weighted BCE-with-logits emphasizes identity-related, toxic, background-toxic, and high-confidence examples; subtype BCE has weight 0.14. A replacement weighted sampler oversamples identity-related and toxic groups. AdamW uses distinct encoder and head learning rates, weight decay, and warmup followed by cosine scheduling. Training supports up to 100 epochs with mixed precision, two-batch gradient accumulation, norm clipping, scheduler updates per optimizer step, checkpoint restoration, and session-controlled early stopping. Toxicity inference applies sigmoid to logits.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Ranking Classifier
summary: The solution predicts comment toxicity with a pretrained ModernBERT-large sequence classifier producing one logit. Raw train/test data are split before preprocessing. Comment text is normalized; standardized length, punctuation, casing and URL features are derived; identity annotations are retained. Benign comments mentioning identities receive higher sample weights, and selected low-toxicity identity comments are augmented by lexical identity swaps while retaining targets. The loss combines sample-weighted soft-target binary cross-entropy with sampled pairwise softplus ranking losses for overall, subgroup, background-positive/subgroup-negative, and subgroup-positive/background-negative comparisons; bias-ranking terms use temperature-scaled log-sum-exp aggregation. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, without weight decay for biases or normalization parameters. Batches are shuffled and tokenized with padding/truncation; mixed precision, gradient accumulation, finite-loss checks, and gradient clipping are supported. Inference sigmoid-transforms batched logits. Checkpoints store weights, configuration, tokenizer, sequence length, activation metadata, and identity-loss columns.

title: ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a ModernBERT-large sequence classifier with one logit for toxicity prediction. It normalizes comments with NFKC and HTML decoding, removes tags and controls, replaces URLs and @mentions with tokens, and collapses whitespace. It also computes standardized text-statistics and identity-keyword features, but the neural dataset and model consume only normalized text. Soft fractional target values are optimized using mean binary cross-entropy with logits; a 0.5 threshold is used only to construct sampling classes. Training retains all positives and at most three negatives per positive, then uses replacement weighted sampling to balance retained classes. Text is tokenized to 256 tokens with dynamic padding to a multiple of eight. AdamW uses 1.5e-5 learning rate and 0.01 decay except biases and normalization weights. Four epochs use batch size 8, four-step gradient accumulation, AMP on CUDA, and gradient clipping at norm 1. Inference applies sigmoid to logits in batches of 32.

title: Identity-aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode- and HTML-normalized, stripped of tags and control characters, with URLs and emails replaced and whitespace collapsed. The implementation also creates identity-masked and standardized style-feature views, although the shown encoder consumes normalized text. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes sequences up to 256 tokens; mean pooling over non-padding tokens feeds a linear, LayerNorm, GELU, and dropout representation, followed by toxicity and subtype heads. Training combines identity-upweighted toxicity binary cross-entropy, finite-label-masked subtype BCE, and pairwise softplus ranking losses for observed identity/background subgroup conditions. A sampler periodically forms batches from benign/toxic subgroup and observed-background pools, otherwise using deterministic epoch shuffling. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates with decay exclusions. Mixed precision, gradient accumulation, unscaled global-norm clipping at 1.0, and scaler updates are used. Inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits and clips probabilities to [0,1]. Checkpoints retain model and preprocessing metadata.

title: Frozen ModernBERT Identity-Aware Toxicity Ranker
summary: The method splits data before preprocessing, normalizes comment text, and computes standardized text-structure features from training statistics. It upweights identity-labelled benign examples and some toxic identity examples, and adds up to 150,000 benign identity-swap counterfactuals retaining targets and weights. A pretrained ModernBERT-large classifier produces one toxicity logit; only its classifier head is optimized. Inputs are tokenized comment text with padding and truncation to length 384, while token-type IDs are removed. Training uses soft toxicity targets, sample weights, and identity values. Its criterion combines weighted binary cross-entropy with sampled pairwise softplus ranking losses for overall and identity-related subgroup/background comparisons, aggregating bias components with temperature-scaled log-sum-exp. AdamW uses 3e-5 learning rate and selective weight decay; AMP, gradient accumulation, unscaled norm-1 clipping, and shuffled batches are supported. Evaluation and test prediction use batched inference and sigmoid logits; checkpoints include weights, configuration, tokenizer, activation, sequence length, and identity columns.

title: Gated ModernBERT Toxicity Prediction
summary: Comments are normalized, with URLs and emails replaced by markers; long text is truncated by retaining head and tail segments. Seventeen robustly scaled structural features capture length, lexical diversity, capitalization, punctuation, digits, quotations, URLs/emails, pronouns, negation, and training-duplicate signals. A ModernBERT-large encoder supplies a first-token representation. An MLP embeds numeric features, whose sigmoid-gated contribution is added before a two-logit prediction head for binary toxicity and a continuous target. Training combines their BCE losses with weights 0.78 and 0.22, and applies identity-by-label group DRO using EMA group losses and softmax weights over active groups. Shuffled batches of 12 are optimized with AdamW, separate backbone/head learning rates, 100-step linear warmup, CUDA mixed precision, gradient scaling, and global gradient-norm clipping to 1.0. A scheduler and session controller advance each batch; training may stop early. Inference blends the sigmoid outputs with the same weights and clips probabilities.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classification with Endpoint Ranking
summary: Comments are NFKC-normalized, HTML-unescaped, stripped of tags and control characters, with URLs and mentions replaced by tokens and whitespace collapsed. Auxiliary standardized text statistics are constructed, while the shown classifier uses cleaned text. A ModernBERT-large sequence classifier outputs one toxicity logit; sigmoid produces probabilities. Soft toxicity targets are trained with BCE-with-logits, with binary labels thresholded at 0.5 for sampling and ranking. Training can combine BCE with pairwise softplus ranking loss using queues of detached logits for identity subgroups and subgroup/background endpoints. A replacement weighted sampler uses inverse binary-class frequencies. AdamW applies 1.5e-5 learning rate and 0.01 weight decay excluding bias and normalization parameters. CUDA mixed precision, four epochs, batch size eight, four-step accumulation, gradient clipping at 1.0, and queued ranking updates are used. Inference tokenizes to length 256, pads longest batches to multiples of eight, and applies sigmoid to batched logits.

title: Identity-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Ranking
summary: Comments are Unicode- and HTML-normalized, with tags and control characters removed, URLs and emails replaced, and whitespace collapsed. An identity-masked text view and standardized style features are created, but training uses normalized text rather than these auxiliary inputs. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes sequences truncated to 256 tokens. Mean pooling over non-padding tokens feeds a linear normalization, GELU, dropout, and output heads for toxicity and six subtypes. The objective combines identity-weighted toxicity BCE, masked BCE for present subtype labels, and softplus pairwise ranking losses between subgroup/background toxic and benign examples. Batches are shuffled, with every fourth eligible batch stratified across four identity/toxicity groups. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates, selective weight decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, clipping at 1.0, and scaler-controlled updates. Inference applies sigmoid toxicity prediction and clips outputs to [0,1]. Checkpoints retain model weights, tokenizer, scaler, length, feature metadata, and prediction semantics.

title: ModernBERT toxicity ranking classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a ModernBERT-large sequence classifier with one regression logit for comment toxicity. Text is NFKC-normalized, HTML-unescaped, stripped of tags/control characters, and has URLs and user mentions replaced with tokens; inputs are tokenized to 256 tokens. It computes textual statistics and regex identity-mention features, standardizing continuous statistics from training data, but the model dataset supplies only cleaned text. Soft toxicity targets are retained, while targets at least 0.5 define binary labels and available identity annotations define masks. Training uses class-balanced sampling with replacement. The loss equally combines BCE-with-logits on soft targets and pairwise softplus ranking losses for overall, within-subgroup, background-positive/subgroup-negative, and subgroup-positive/background-negative binary pairs. AdamW uses 1.5e-5 learning rate, selective 0.01 weight decay, mixed precision, four-step gradient accumulation, and norm clipping at 1.0 for up to four epochs. Inference returns sigmoid probabilities from batched model logits.

title: Selective ModernBERT Toxicity Ranking Classifier
summary: The solution preprocesses comment text with Unicode normalization, control/HTML removal, and URL/email markers, and derives structural text features. It uses toxicity targets, fairness weights, and identity annotations; benign identity examples are upweighted and selected identity mentions can be counterfactually swapped, with counterfactual identity values set to NaN. A ModernBERT-large classifier outputs one toxicity logit. All parameters are frozen except the classification head, final encoder block, and final normalization. Training optimizes weighted soft-label binary cross-entropy plus sampled pairwise logistic ranking losses for overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP comparisons; bias components are combined by temperature-scaled log-sum-exp. Batches are shuffled, tokenized with truncation and padding, and omit token-type IDs. AdamW uses separate head/backbone learning rates and excludes bias and normalization parameters from weight decay. CUDA AMP, gradient accumulation, scaling, unscaling, and norm clipping are used. Batched inference applies sigmoid; checkpoints save model, tokenizer, configuration, sequence length, identity columns, and prediction activation.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Ranker
summary: Text is NFKC-normalized, with URLs, emails, IP addresses, and user mentions replaced by special tokens. Missing comments are converted to empty strings. Identity membership masks and identity-by-target cells are derived for reweighting and ranking. A pretrained ModernBERT-large classifier, resized for the added tokens, maps tokenized text (maximum 256 tokens) to one toxicity logit. Training combines dynamically reweighted BCE with pairwise softplus ranking losses for overall, within-identity, and cross-group positive/negative comparisons. Cell-level point-loss EMAs determine clipped sample weights. The backbone can be frozen for head warm-up and then unfrozen. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning-rate/decay groups, with shuffled batches, mixed precision, gradient scaling, accumulation, and global-norm clipping. Checkpoints retain model, criterion, tokenizer, encoder configuration, preprocessing state, and sequence settings. Evaluation and inference return sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Counterfactual-consistent DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a two-class DeBERTa-v3-large classifier for continuous toxicity targets, using the difference between toxic and non-toxic logits and a sigmoid probability. It cleans comment text by normalizing Unicode, removing HTML, replacing URLs/emails, limiting repeated characters, and truncating tokenized inputs to 256 tokens. Identity and toxicity metadata are retained; training identities are thresholded at 0.5. Although standardized handcrafted text features are computed and saved, model inputs are text only. Embeddings and all but the last four encoder layers are frozen. The loss is binary cross-entropy plus, for benign examples containing official identity labels, a weighted squared difference between predictions for original and identity-neutralized text. Training shuffles examples for up to three epochs with AdamW, separate encoder-tail/head learning rates, selective weight decay, mixed precision when CUDA is available, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, and session-controlled early stopping. Inference batches text, applies sigmoid toxicity probabilities, and supports checkpoint save/load.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Text is cleaned by replacing URLs and emails, removing HTML/control characters, limiting repeated characters, and extracting standardized numeric features. A pretrained ModernBERT encodes padded, truncated comments; masked mean-pooled embeddings are fused with numeric-feature representations for toxicity, subtype, and identity prediction. The identity branch uses gradient reversal. Training combines toxicity BCE, masked subtype BCE, benign-example identity BCE, and sampled pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP slices, with temperature-controlled log-sum-exp group aggregation. Each epoch visits all examples and adds 20% replacement samples from identity-labelled comments. AdamW uses encoder-specific lower learning rates and differential weight decay, CUDA mixed precision, gradient scaling, and gradient clipping. Inference evaluates selected positions without gradients, applies sigmoid to toxicity logits, and restores model state. Checkpoints retain weights, tokenizer, configuration, and preprocessing artifacts.

title: Counterfactual Identity-Neutralized Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a two-logit DeBERTa-v3-base classifier for continuous toxicity targets. It cleans comments by normalizing Unicode, removing HTML, replacing URLs/emails, compressing repeated characters, and standardizing whitespace. It also derives standardized text-count and ratio features, but the shown model input uses only tokenized cleaned text. Embeddings and all but the final four encoder layers are frozen. Training uses binary cross-entropy on the difference between toxic and non-toxic logits. For benign examples with annotated official identity membership, it creates a second input by replacing identity terms with an identity placeholder and adds a 0.35-weighted squared difference between original and neutralized toxicity probabilities. AdamW uses layer-specific learning rates, decoupled weight decay excluding bias/normalization parameters, mixed precision where available, gradient accumulation, and norm clipping. Inference tokenizes cleaned comments to 128 tokens and returns sigmoid logit-difference probabilities.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Ranker
summary: Comments are Unicode-normalized and URLs, emails, IP addresses, and user mentions are replaced by special tokens. Standardized text statistics and identity/target masks are derived, while the shown neural classifier uses tokenized text. A pretrained ModernBERT sequence classifier extended with the replacement tokens outputs a toxicity margin, computed as the positive-minus-negative logit when two logits are present. Binary cross-entropy is weighted dynamically using exponential moving averages of loss in 18 identity-by-label cells, formed from nine identities and positive or non-positive targets. Weights use relative cell risk raised to 1.5 and are clipped to 0.35–3.0. AdamW applies separate encoder and head learning rates and decay groups. Training uses shuffled batches for up to three epochs, four-step gradient accumulation, CUDA AMP when available, gradient clipping, epoch loss aggregation, validation tracking, and an epoch-level stop flag. Inference truncates inputs to 256 tokens and applies a sigmoid to the margin.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution preprocesses comments by normalizing text, replacing URLs and emails, removing markup/control characters, limiting repeated characters, and deriving 13 standardized text-statistic, identity-lexicon, and training-frequency features. A pretrained ModernBERT encoder mean-pools masked token embeddings and combines them with an MLP encoding numeric features to predict toxicity and six subtypes. An adversarial identity head uses gradient reversal on the shared representation. Training uses BCE for toxicity, masked subtype and benign-example identity losses, plus sampled subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP pairwise ranking losses across nine identities with robust temperature-smoothed aggregation. Each epoch covers all examples and adds 20% replacement samples from identity-present cases. Initially only heads train; later the final four encoder blocks are unfrozen. AdamW uses separate encoder learning rates, selective weight decay, AMP, and gradient clipping. Inference sigmoid-transforms the toxicity logit.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Ranker
summary: Comment text is normalized with NFKC and HTML unescaping; URLs, emails, IP addresses and usernames are replaced with placeholders, then whitespace is collapsed. A pretrained ModernBERT-large classifier, extended with these placeholders, produces a toxicity margin by subtracting the negative-class logit from the positive-class logit. Training uses clipped continuous targets and per-example binary cross-entropy. Identity-by-target masks define 18 cells whose EMA losses determine relative-risk weights, clipped to 0.35–3.0; each sample receives the mean weight of its active cells. Shuffled batches use dynamic padding and 256-token truncation. AdamW applies separate encoder and head learning rates and decay groups; the encoder is frozen initially and unfrozen after a configured number of optimizer updates. CUDA mixed precision, four-step gradient accumulation, unscaled global gradient clipping at 1.0, and scaler-based updates are used. A controller may stop training early. Inference applies sigmoid to the margin.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Model with Structural Features
summary: The solution cleans comment text and computes 16 scaled structural features covering length, casing, character ratios, punctuation, URLs, mentions, and repeated punctuation. A pretrained ModernBERT-large encoder, with gradient checkpointing, produces CLS and attention-mask mean-pooled representations; their projection is concatenated with an MLP projection of the structural features to predict one toxicity logit. Labels include soft toxicity, masked subtype and identity annotations, and hard thresholds for identity-based strata. Eligible single-identity comments may undergo constrained identity-term replacement during training. The loss combines optionally weighted soft-target binary cross-entropy with a pairwise logistic ranking loss, including overall and subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP identity comparisons; identity losses are smooth-max aggregated, and ranking has weight 0.20. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, excluded decay parameters, mixed precision, clipping, accumulation, warm-up, and finite-loss checks. A no-replacement sampler seeks identity/label-stratified batches. Inference tokenizes truncated text, applies sigmoid probabilities, and retries with smaller batches after CUDA memory errors.

title: Dual-view sparse toxicity classifier
summary: The solution cleans comment text and creates a debiased view by replacing matched identity terms with category placeholders. It builds hashed binary word unigram/bigram features for both views, clean-text character 3–5-grams, and training-standardized numeric style features. Sparse fields are encoded by embedding-bag latent and wide paths. Debiased word and numeric features form a base representation, character features add context, and a gated bounded residual from original words is fused for the full prediction. Heads produce toxicity, subtype and identity outputs; identity prediction uses gradient reversal on contextual features. Training uses weighted BCE for full and debiased toxicity, masked weighted subtype and identity losses, consistency for non-toxic identity examples, and ranking losses overall and for subgroup, BPSN and BNSP slices. Sparse parameters use Adagrad and remaining parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped. Shuffled batches run up to three epochs. Inference returns sigmoid full-toxicity probabilities.

title: Fairness-Aware Sparse Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system normalizes comments by replacing URLs, emails, mentions and identity terms, then builds hashed word 1–2-gram, character 3–5-gram and standardized style features. Weighted EmbeddingBag components encode sparse inputs; debiased-word and numeric features provide a base representation, character features add context, and original-word features are incorporated through a sigmoid gate with a bounded residual. It predicts toxicity and optional subtype outputs, with a gradient-reversal identity classifier to encourage identity-invariant context. Training combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, non-toxic identity consistency and hard pairwise ranking losses for overall and identity slices. Slice-loss EMAs update robust weights using multiplicative updates and capped-simplex projection. Replay reservoirs supply examples missing from ranking slices. Sparse parameters use Adagrad and dense parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped and non-finite-loss batches skipped. Inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits.

title: Dual-View Sparse Debiased Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized by decoding HTML/Unicode, masking URLs, emails and mentions, removing tags/control characters and canonicalizing simple obfuscation. The pipeline builds clean and identity-masked text, then concatenates hashed word unigram/bigram features from both views, clean character 3–5-grams, and standardized style features. A sparse neural model encodes word and character fields with weighted EmbeddingBag latent and wide-logit components. Debiased words and numeric features form a base state; characters add context, while original words contribute through a sigmoid gate and bounded residual. It predicts toxicity and subtypes, with an identity adversary connected through gradient reversal. The loss combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked weighted subtype and identity BCE, consistency between full and debiased predictions for non-toxic identity examples, and hard ranking losses for overall and identity-derived slices. Replay reservoirs add missing slice sides to training batches. Sparse parameters use Adagrad and dense parameters AdamW; dense gradients are clipped. Inference returns sigmoid-transformed full toxicity logits.

title: Adversarial ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text and derives 16 standardized structural features. It uses masked soft toxicity, subtype, and identity labels, thresholds hard labels at 0.5, and identifies eligible identity-term replacements. A ModernBERT-large encoder combines CLS and masked-mean token embeddings, projects semantic and structural features, and produces a toxicity logit. A gradient-reversal head predicts nine identity labels from semantic features, with masked BCE weighted toward benign comments. The objective combines soft-target BCE with sampled pairwise logistic ranking losses for overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP slices, using a smooth maximum across identity families. Training can replace identity terms, uses identity-stratified batches, AdamW groups, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, warm-up scheduling, and a step-ramped adversarial coefficient. Inference applies sigmoid and retries smaller CUDA batches after memory errors. Checkpoints include model, tokenizer, scaler, and settings.

title: Counterfactual Chunked DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comments, computes standardized numeric text and lexicon features, and builds soft toxicity, auxiliary subtype, and masked identity targets with toxicity/identity-aware sample weights. It augments selected identity-labelled comments through deterministic identity-term counterfactual swaps, reducing their weights. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large encoder processes 256-token chunks; chunk representations combine CLS and masked learned-attention pooling, then chunk attention aggregates them. Numeric features pass through an MLP and are fused with text features. General toxicity logits are dropout-averaged; subtype and identity heads are jointly trained, and subtype mechanism weights can combine subtype probabilities with the general prediction. The objective includes weighted main BCE, masked auxiliary losses, identity-slice balanced losses, score-gap penalties, and mechanism regularization. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, mixed precision, accumulation, clipping, checkpointing, and early stopping. Inference outputs clipped sigmoid probabilities.

title: Identity-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: A ModernBERT-large toxicity classifier combines CLS and masked mean token embeddings with standardized structural text features. Comments are conservatively cleaned; 16 features capture length, casing, character types, punctuation, URLs, emails, mentions, and repeated punctuation. Soft toxicity, subtype, and identity labels use missing-label masks, while thresholds define identity metric strata. The scalar logit is trained with weighted soft-target BCE and identity-sliced pairwise logistic ranking losses, including sampled within-batch pairs and detached per-identity historical-logit buffers. Slice losses cover subgroup, background-positive/subgroup-negative, and subgroup-positive/background-negative cases, with smooth-max identity aggregation. Eligible uniquely identified comments may receive identity-term substitutions while retaining toxicity targets and updating batch-local strata. A stratified sampler seeds batches from metric slices. AdamW uses distinct backbone/head rates, no decay for bias or normalization parameters, warmup, mixed precision, gradient accumulation and clipping. Inference applies sigmoid probabilities, with reduced batch-size retry after CUDA memory errors.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Structural Features
summary: Comments are conservatively cleaned, tokenized to 256 tokens, and augmented with 16 standardized structural features covering length, character ratios, punctuation, URLs, emails, and mentions. ModernBERT-large produces CLS and masked-mean embeddings; their projection is concatenated with an MLP projection of structural features and passed through dropout to a scalar logit. Training uses soft-target BCE, optionally weighted, plus sampled logistic ranking losses over overall, subgroup, and identity-related positive/negative slices, with identity-family losses combined by a smooth maximum. Hard toxicity and scored identity labels are masked when unavailable; identities are objective-only inputs. A sampler periodically seeks identity-stratified batches while covering rows without replacement. AdamW separates backbone/head learning rates, uses warmup, selective weight decay, clipping, AMP, gradient accumulation, and scheduler steps only after applied updates. Inference applies sigmoid and retries with smaller batches after CUDA OOM.

title: Chunk-attentive DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: Text is normalized (Unicode, punctuation, markup, URLs, emails and handles) and paired with standardized style, lexical, identity and hostility features. A deterministic split is used. Training weights emphasize toxic and identity-annotated examples, particularly rare identities. Selected identity examples receive hash-selected, case-preserving identity-swap counterfactuals with transformed identity labels and 0.70 weight. Long text retains beginning and end around a middle marker. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large encoder, with only its top eight layers trainable, uses first-token plus masked attention pooling, chunk attention, numeric-feature MLP fusion, and dropout-averaged toxicity heads; subtype and identity heads are auxiliary. Final toxicity combines general and subtype non-toxicity through learned nonnegative weights. The loss includes weighted main BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, identity subgroup/background smooth-max terms, identity probability-gap penalties, and mechanism regularization. AdamW, warmup-cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation, clipping and finite-value checks are used. Inference outputs clipped finite sigmoid probabilities.

title: Slice-aware DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: Comments undergo Unicode, HTML, punctuation and placeholder normalization, then standardized numeric feature extraction. Training data is split before fitting transforms. Identity-annotated rows can generate deterministic hash-selected counterfactual identity-word swaps, retaining targets and features but using swapped identity labels and 0.70 weight. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder with frozen embeddings/lower layers pools CLS and attention-weighted tokens; valid chunks are attention-combined. Projected numeric features are fused with text features. Heads predict toxicity, subtypes and identities; four dropout toxicity passes are averaged, and learned positive subtype weights may combine probabilities. The loss includes weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, smooth-max balanced subgroup/BPSN/BNSP slice losses, gap penalties and weight regularization. AdamW uses separate backbone/head rates, selective decay, AMP, checkpointing, accumulation, clipping, and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference applies identical preprocessing, sigmoid outputs and probability clipping.

title: Dual-view latent-rationale toxicity classifier
summary: The solution normalizes text, replaces entities such as URLs and mentions with special tokens, and derives numeric style, abuse, identity and discourse features. It creates primary text and a quote-masked alternate view, standardizes numeric features on training data, and weights examples for duplicates and annotator counts. A ModernBERT encoder, extended with custom tokens, produces token embeddings. Evidence and relevance heads generate token toxicity scores and masked attention, whose weighted embedding is fused with the first-token representation and numeric-feature tower. Global and bag-level toxicity logits are combined through a learned gate; additional heads predict beta-binomial concentration and subtypes. Training uses weighted beta-binomial and binary losses, bag and subtype losses, subgroup disparity regularization, alternate-view consistency, and gate regularization. AdamW applies layerwise backbone learning-rate decay, warmup/cosine scheduling, AMP, accumulation and clipping. Length-grouped shuffled batches are used. Inference averages primary and changed alternate-view probabilities, then sanitizes and clips outputs.

title: Dual-View Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution predicts toxicity probabilities from paired original and identity-masked comments plus standardized numeric text features. Comments are normalized for markup, whitespace, URLs, emails, mentions and controls; a fixed identity lexicon is replaced with an identity token in the masked view. It derives 22 stylistic features, fits scaling only on training data, uses clipped soft toxicity labels, and constructs subtype, identity and counterfactual metadata. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT-large encodes both 256-token views; first-token and masked-mean pooling are combined. A GELU numeric encoder and gated dual-view fusion produce toxicity, subtype and gradient-reversed identity predictions. Training uses weighted toxicity BCE, branch BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, adversarial identity BCE, view consistency, pairwise ranking, and worst-group ranking losses. AdamW applies separate backbone/head settings, AMP, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, warmup-cosine scheduling, and partial-window correction. Inference tokenizes paired views, applies sigmoid to main logits, and clips outputs to [0,1].

title: Sparse Wide-Deep Toxicity Predictor
summary: Comment text is normalized by replacing URLs, emails, IP addresses and usernames, then represented with hashed word 1–2-grams, character 3–5-grams, and standardized dense style, lexical, identity and context features. CSR features are converted to embedding-bag indices, values and offsets. A wide sparse logit and normalized, dropout-regularized deep pooled embeddings are combined with an optional dense tower and shared GELU layers. Heads predict toxicity, subtypes and identities; a gradient-reversed adversarial identity head uses toxicity features and the wide logit. Training uses fractional toxicity labels, cell-balanced and uncertainty-aware sample weights, and batches augmented from identity-by-binary-toxicity cells. Losses include weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCEs, adversarial BCE, representation decorrelation, and subgroup/BPSN/BNSP ranking losses with soft worst-group aggregation. Embeddings use Adagrad; remaining parameters use AdamW, warmup-cosine schedules, adversarial ramping and gradient clipping. Inference sigmoids and clips toxicity probabilities.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The system cleans toxicity comments, tokenizes them with ModernBERT-large, and derives standardized numeric text and lexicon features. Identity spans detected from token offsets are removed in a neutral pooling mask. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT encodes tokens once; original and neutral pooled views are gated, fused with an MLP representation of numeric features, and projected to toxicity logits. Auxiliary heads predict toxicity subtypes and identities, with gradient reversal for identity-adversarial training. Identity-conditioned batches balance toxic/non-toxic subgroup and background examples. Training uses weighted soft-label BCE, view consistency, ranking surrogates, and smooth worst-group losses. Only the final backbone layers and normalization are trainable. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates, warmup followed by cosine decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference applies sigmoid and clips toxicity probabilities.

title: Dual-View Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The pipeline cleans comments and creates an identity-masked text view. It derives standardized text statistics, fitting the scaler on training data only, and retains soft toxicity, subtype, and identity labels. A partially fine-tuned ModernBERT encodes original and masked text; pooled representations and a GELU numeric-feature encoder are fused through a gated counterfactual representation for toxicity and subtype prediction. A gradient-reversal identity head promotes identity-invariant features. The loss combines weighted soft-label toxicity BCE, view-specific BCE, masked subtype/identity BCE, counterfactual consistency, and pairwise ranking losses for overall and identity-related groups with smooth worst-group aggregation. Epoch-seeded identity-quadrant sampling balances subgroup/background and positive/negative examples. AdamW uses separate backbone and head rates, warmup-cosine scheduling, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, and checkpointing. Inference batches indexed examples, applies sigmoid to main logits, and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Identity-aware DeBERTa toxicity classifier
summary: The model tokenizes comment text and combines DeBERTa-v3-large representations with numeric features. It uses pooled non-identity evidence and an identity-aware branch based on detected identity-token spans and surrounding context, then predicts toxicity alongside auxiliary, evidence and concentration outputs. Training data include soft toxicity labels, masked auxiliary labels, annotator counts, identity/context values and sample weights. Metric-cell-balanced sortish sampling uses approximate sequence length, targets and identity groups. The joint criterion consumes primary, concentration, auxiliary, sentence-evidence and token-evidence logits, corresponding labels and masks, identity-token masks, annotator counts and weights. Mixed-precision optimization accumulates gradients, clips their norm to 1.0 and uses AdamW-style updates with warmup followed by cosine learning-rate decay.
